correctness.rationale: Group-absence indicator covariance gives an exact rational expression valid at all sample budgets, including endpoints. The standard-library verifier exhausts all 259 nontrivial integer partitions of totals 2..12 and all 100 nontrivial partitions of total 13; only (1,6,6) fails unimodality, independently checked by complete direct enumeration of all size-k survivor subsets. The infinite (1,m,m) family follows analytically from a positive polynomial for V_3-V_4 and a binomial coefficient lower bound for V_m-V_(m-1); finite tests merely corroborate the universal proof. Limits: idealized disjoint groups and uniform fixed-count survival.

originality.rationale: Heck et al. (1975) and Fonseca--Ganade (2001) already give the general conditional richness-variance calculation, which is not claimed novel. The new result determines the exact smallest non-unimodal total, the unique exceptional group-size partition at that total, and a proved infinite family of non-unimodal curves. Examined full-text ecological and infinite-urn treatments did not state or imply a ready-made shape classification. The inaccessible 1975 primary full text and possible unindexed rarefaction shape results remain real priority risks.
residual_risks: The full primary text of Heck, van Belle and Simberloff (1975) was inaccessible, and contains the general variance formula; a prior shape example or calculation cannot be excluded.
Earlier rarefaction and finite-urn literature may contain equivalent non-unimodality examples under different terminology.

The minimality certificate relies on a finite exact-arithmetic implementation whose exhaustive partition generator is documented and independently spot-checked, rather than a human enumerating all 359 profiles.

value.rationale: A natural ecological functional-redundancy statistic can have more than one separate uncertainty peak as extinctions proceed; the exact first size and uniqueness are intrinsic cutoff questions, not a chosen arbitrary slice. The all-m>=6 proof explains persistence of that phenomenon structurally. A single-peak confidence heuristic for fixed-budget monitoring is therefore unsafe even in a simple widely used model. The result does not purport to predict empirical ecological stability.
